newsitem.title: USA: Thai yankee bonds firm in U.S. on technical bounce.
newsitem.headline: Thai yankee bonds firm in U.S. on technical bounce.

text.p: Prices of Thai yankee bonds halted their recent slide after the Bank of Thailand let the baht float, U.S. market sources said.

The spread of the benchmark 10-year Kingdom of Thailand yankee tightened by some 10 basis points to bid 98/99 over comparable U.S. Treasury securties. The spread had traded as wide as 106/107, they said.
The effective 15-percent devaluation as a result of the floatation was generally seen as positive for the Thai economy, which has been reeling from high interest rates and economic crises.
Issued at 90 base points over U.S. Treasury on April 10, spreads tightened to 82 basis points before going into their unremitting slide, traders said.
Looking beyond the technical bounce, traders expected the volatility of Thai papers to remain high.
"Thailand still has to sort out many problems," said a trader.
Prices for Philippine yankees were basically unchanged, even though the peso came under pressure after the baht floated, trading sources said.
Phillipine yankees have been a bigger disapointment for investors, as their spread has deteriorated faster than that of the troubled Thai papers.
At 184.5 basis points for the 30-year tranche, the spread was widely considered as too tight at the launch on June 19. It widened to over 200 basis points in just two weeks.
The benchmark 30-year bond was bid 203 basis points over Treasuries, which was unchanged from Monday, the trading sources said.
The paper was rated Ba1 by Moody's and BB-plus by S&P.
